messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-cluster-2 GPU queue growth > 500% in 5m. avg token wait 2.3s -> 12s. ASG scale attempts failing. link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/pgpu/gpu-queues?orgId=1 :rotating_light:
Chris H: taking pager. looking at autoscaler logs now. tag @ops_oncall for handoff if needed.
ops_oncall: oncall here, taking. adding context in thread.
Maya G: I see repeated errors from cluster-autoscaler: 
```
E1001 14:02:11.123456 1 utils.go:123] Failed to create instance: LaunchTemplateVersionNotFound: version 5 for lt-0abcd1234 not found
status code: 400, request id: 6f4c...
```
Also IAM error intermittently: instance profile 'redwood-gpu-node' not attached to LT v4.
Ravi P: that would explain nodes not joining -> queue backs up. Are ASG desired attempts failing or is AWS rejecting the LT?
Maya G: AWS is rejecting create, autoscaler retries but ASG reports "CapacityNotAvailable" and also we hit per-region OnDemand vCPU quota for particular family. There are a couple of failures: LT version mismatch + instance profile misconfig + regional quota.
Chris H: customer impact? any 5xxs? which routes?
Emma L: partial: embedding/async-rerank queues are piling. We see increased 429s from the frontend because the request queue length is exceeding backend capacity. Affected tenants: org-23, org-57, org-99 (lightly), roughly 12 customers with degraded tails. 95th latency for text-generation up from 1.1s -> 4.2s.
ops_oncall: immediate mitigation ideas? Can we fallback to smaller models or degrade non-critical routes?
Ravi P: pushing model downgrade for non-SLA routes now (degraded model mapping) — rolling to 3 hosts to cut GPU usage.
Maya G: I'll try manual scale: create a temporary ASG with a new Launch Template version that has the proper instance profile and updated user-data to install nvidia drivers earlier. If quota blocks OnDemand, we can try a mixed instances policy and include a larger range of allowed instance types.
Chris H: go for manual ASG, keep autoscaler paused for the affected nodegroup to avoid fight. Add an annotation to avoid autoscaler deleting nodes while we provision.
Maya G: Commands I ran (console copy):
```
aws ec2 create-launch-template-version --launch-template-id lt-0abcd1234 --source-version 4 --launch-template-data '{"IamInstanceProfile":{"Name":"redwood-gpu-node"},"UserData":"...encoded..."}'
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name redwood-temp-gpu-2026 --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd1234,Version=5 --min-size 1 --max-size 10 --desired-capacity 3 --mixed-instances-policy '...'
```
Maya G: infra-bot: tagging new ASG with project=redwood, incident=2018709999.
infra-bot: Created ASG redwood-temp-gpu-2026 (3 instances asked). Initial instance launch slow due to bootstrapping (scripts + driver install).
Ravi P: started model routing changes. non-critical jobs switched off GPU fallback to CPU (best-effort). Should reduce queue by ~30%.
Chris H: customer comms? Emma?
Emma L: drafting note for affected customers, will send an initial alert with ETA ~30-45m. CC on PM/Success.
Maya G: New nodes are launching but one instance failed user-data step and is stuck NotReady due to nvidia driver install timeout. Logs show kernel mismatch; working on baking a fixed AMI.
Ravi P: can we mark the node as unschedulable and let it drain? We need healthy nodes.
Maya G: marking Unhealthy and cycling. Creating AMI now from a successful instance and updating LT v6.
Chris H: autoscaler status?
Maya G: autoscaler still trying original nodegroup but failing because the Launch Template there points at v4 which doesn't have the instance profile. I've set cluster-autoscaler to skip that nodegroup (--skip-nodes-with-local-storage?) and increased --balance-similar-node-groups to false temporarily to avoid oscillation.
ops_oncall: good. Ops handoff: I'm going offline in 20m; handing to Ravi P. Ravi, you're primary until 16:30 UTC.
Ravi P: got it. I'll watch ASG scaling and traffic.
Emma L: customer note sent to impacted tenants, flagged as "service degradation".
Maya G: AMI baked and LT v6 published. Updated temporary ASG to use v6. New nodes came up healthy and joined cluster. GPU capacity now ~80% of baseline; queue drains slowly.
Chris H: metrics: queue length back to 1.2x baseline after routing + temp ASG. 95th latency down to 1.6s. Not fully recovered but improving.
Emma L: customer follow-up: initial ETA met, proactive outreach to top impacted customers, asked SEs to prioritize any urgent jobs.
Chris H: next steps (short):
- Maya: replace broken nodegroup LT with v6 and ensure instance profile attached (owner infra)
- Ravi: keep monitoring autoscaler & ASG quotas, revert model downgrade when stable (owner runtime)
- Emma: follow-up comms and create incident severity classification (owner support)
- Chris: write postmortem template and start timeline capture (owner oncall)
Maya G: I'll also open a request with cloud to increase OnDemand quota for GPU family; file number in infra ticket.
Chris H: tagging for postmortem: @Maya G @Ravi P @Emma L. Closing pager for now, keep channel open for updates. :white_check_mark:
ops_oncall: handoff acknowledged. Leaving note: last_check 15:58 UTC - queue stable-ish.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Chris H.
Chris H: leaving final note before stepping out: remediated via temp ASG and LT version fix, root cause = mismatched launch template version + missing IAM instance profile + regional OnDemand quota exhaustion leading autoscaler creates to be rejected. Postmortem to include why LT drifted and why CI didn't catch instance profile removal.
Emma L: I'll schedule customer follow-ups and add remediation timeline to the incident doc.
Ravi P: will monitor for 2h and escalate if any regressions.
Chris H: thanks team.
